threads.body: [Testing] The ending instrumenter has no listener, so this only proves that the start listener can be carried to an otherwise empty instrumenter. It would still pass if `doEnd()` called both the propagated listeners and the ending instrumenter's listeners. Could you add a distinct listener to `endingInstrumenter` and assert that it is not called? That would directly verify the intended listener-selection behavior.

replies.body: Thanks, good point. I added a separate listener to the ending instrumenter and verify that it is not called, so the test now checks that `end()` uses only the listener propagated from `start()`.

[Testing] Setting the package-private `propagateOperationListenersToOnEnd` field directly bypasses the API that real callers use. The test above already goes through `InstrumenterUtil.propagateOperationListenersToOnEnd(...)` — using it here too keeps both tests on the same path and drops the extra builder local.

```suggestion
    Instrumenter<Map<String, String>, Map<String, String>> parentInstrumenter =
        InstrumenterUtil.propagateOperationListenersToOnEnd(
                Instrumenter.<Map<String, String>, Map<String, String>>builder(
                        otelTesting.getOpenTelemetry(), "test", unused -> "span")
                    .addOperationListener(parentOperationListener))
            .buildServerInstrumenter(new MapGetter());
```

replies.body: Added assertions confirming the child does not end the parent listener and the parent’s own `end()` does.
